end.summary:
Sequenced the East India Company’s rise from trader to ruler: Charter, Plassey, Buxar and Crown rule.
Explained how British cloth contributed to the decline of Indian weaving and craft towns.
Discussed high revenue demands, borrowing, crop failure and loss of land.
Identified indigo cultivation in Champaran and connected low food-crop production with shortages.
Teach-back was not passed; the drain of wealth and full economic impact need further practice.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the Company’s timeline and used examples to explain the decline of Indian textiles. Zoya explained the effects on weavers and connected high revenue, debt and crop failure; the Champaran-indigo point was revisited and confirmed later. The economic effects were not yet explained as a complete chain, especially the drain of wealth. At home, Zoya can make a four-part flow chart: revenue demands, decline of crafts, cash crops, and famines/drain of wealth.
